topic:
Sharp honest interval-length frontier for four-exposure multiple-randomization experiments. For every even n>=4 independently select n/2 buyers and n/2 sellers uniformly from n each. A fixed schedule consists of four matrices Y^gamma in [-2,2]^(n x n), gamma=(tr,ib,is,cc), satisfying exposure consistency under the published local-interference model. Observe assignments and exactly one Y^gamma_ij per pair. Fix direct-effect contrast c=(1,-1,-1,1). Target tau=n^-2 sum_ij sum_gamma c_gamma Y^gamma_ij. Let tauhat be the contrast of four observed block means. Let r=(2W_B-1)*sqrt((n-1)/n), s analogous, so Cov(r)=Cov(s)=P_n=I-11^T/n. Expand uniquely tauhat-tau=a^T r+b^T s+r^T C s with centered a,b and P_n C P_n=C. Define Vplus=(sum_gamma |c_gamma| sqrt(Var_design(Ybarhat_gamma)))^2, precisely source equation 41. Its four component variances are population design quantities, not assumed known to the procedure. For rho in [0,1], F_n(rho) consists of all such schedules with Vplus>=1/(100 n^2), ||C||op/sqrt(Vplus)<=rho, and max_i,j{|a_i|,|b_j|,||C_i.||2,||C_.j||2}/sqrt(Vplus)<=n^(-1/8). Empty finitely many F_n do not define asymptotic claims; show eventual nonemptiness. No assumed CLT, observed spectral profile, variance consistency at chaos boundary, or counterfactual covariance is supplied. For fixed alpha in (0,1/4) define H_alpha(rho) as all sequences of data-measurable (optionally independently randomized) closed intervals I_n with liminf_even n inf_{Y in F_n(rho)} Pr_Y(tau(Y) in I_n)>=1-alpha. Determine the exact asymptotic decision value R_alpha(rho)=inf_{(I_n) in H_alpha(rho)} limsup_even n sup_{Y in F_n(rho)} E_Y length(I_n)/sqrt(Vplus(Y)) for every rho in [0,1], and construct a finite data-computable sequence attaining it, or epsilon-attaining for every epsilon>0, with a matching lower bound against all intervals on the same four-schedule observation experiment. Establish the alignment-aware low-influence Gaussian-chaos approximation needed for the interval and characterize the Gaussian limit boundary. The curve, its possible flatness, and whether Gaussian versus finite-rank interactions change the optimal constant are answers to derive, not assumed conclusions. An exact characterization by a limiting variational problem counts only if accompanied by a convergent finite evaluation algorithm with certified error; restating the original infimum, Chebyshev intervals without sharpness, or declaring Gaussian replacement the main result does not complete the kernel. Explicit interval from the observed four-block table; finite calibration algorithm with a proved convergence/error certificate for any limiting optimization. Full potential outcomes, true Vplus, and unobserved cross-world covariances cannot be inputs. Numerical integration or finite optimization is allowed; exact algorithm and complexity are outputs. Novelty is the sharp observed-data frontier, not Gaussian approximation, a generic finite LP, or conservative intervals alone. Consumers are published MRD marketplace inference and Liu–Shaikh–Toulis's Comola–Prina savings-network reanalysis; the square-half design is an idealized benchmark. Primary sources and exact assumptions are recorded in <repo-root>/internal/topic_selection_20260909_novel2/candidate_final.json.

PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The presolve derived the exact four-exposure linear-plus-bilinear decomposition and variance identity, a quantitative balanced-slice-to-Gaussian replacement preserving shared coordinates, and a certified rank truncation. An interval computed from observed block row and column standard deviations has finite-sample honesty and expected length bounded by a loose constant times the population Neyman envelope. A canceled single-row schedule proves that this envelope cannot be uniformly estimated in relative error even at rho=0; therefore plug-in spectral calibration is not justified. Finite assignment enumeration checked decomposition, moment identities, and the non-Gaussian witness. A hypergeometric lower-benchmark transfer is only sketched. Current MRD, multiway-clustering, and one-population minimax sources did not supply the exact requested frontier. None of this proves the sharp curve.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Construct explicit finite completion games retaining unobserved potential-outcome ambiguity and irregular component nuisance, and prove both uniform observable-policy attainment and same-experiment all-interval lower transfer with a computable vanishing error.
EARLY KILL TEST: At n=8,12 and rho=0,.5,.8,1 compare certified interval LPs on admissible hypergeometric, aligned-interaction, and canceled-nuisance families with quantized-data upper policies. Equal statistic profiles with different decision values reject a profile-only reduction; preserve the full experiment or pivot that route. Drop only for an affirmative collision, generic reduction, or obstruction to every route.
STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/exp_mrd_spectral_honest_length_frontier.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the exact minimax worst-case expected-length frontier R_alpha(rho) for honest intervals for the four-exposure total-effect contrast under balanced simple multiple randomization.

source_refs.claim: SMRD theory gives exact component variances, conservative variance estimators, and Gaussian inference, while cross-exposure covariances remain jointly unobserved.
source_refs.author: Lorenzo Masoero, Suhas Vijaykumar, Thomas S. Richardson, James McQueen, Ido Rosen, Brian Burdick, Pat Bajari, and Guido Imbens

The unrestricted all-rule frontier collapses to one on an admissible boundary class

open_problems.why_unsolved: Published MRD inference supplies conservative Wald intervals rather than the value of the decision problem over all observed-data interval policies. One observed exposure per buyer-seller pair leaves cross-world covariance, irregular additive nuisance, and interaction alignment unidentified. The prior Neyman-jackknife run also shows that an apparent all-rule lower bound can collapse on an admissible boundary when a richer observable proxy reveals the nuisance. Thus neither a Gaussian submodel nor an oracle variance calculation establishes the required frontier without a nuisance-rich full-experiment converse and an observable attaining policy.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit formula or limiting saddle-point problem for R_alpha(rho), with matching upper and all-interval lower bounds and a finite certified algorithm whose values converge to the frontier.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves directly from marketplace interference to four exposure means and the inferential obstruction created by multiple randomizations.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Ordinary A/B tests cannot separate marketplace spillovers -> SMRD produces four interpretable exposure means -> existing conservative inference does not quantify optimal interval length -> determine the exact honest frontier under unobserved covariance and interaction.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the Ghosh-Pratt identity and Bayes-minimax duality to convert worst-case expected interval length into a game over acceptance functions and least-favourable distributions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: R_alpha(rho) has the same coverage-constrained expected-measure loss, with the MRD completion experiment replacing a location family.

method_exemplars.technique: Optimize unidentified cross-world covariance through sharp coupling bounds and estimate the resulting observable endpoints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest finite-population precedent for converting missing cross-world covariance into a sharp inferential benchmark.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert randomization tests after maximizing over sharp potential-outcome completions compatible with the observations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It preserves assignment-only randomness and missing potential outcomes, which any honest MRD policy must respect.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a finite observed-table completion game whose primal policies are honest four-exposure MRD intervals and whose dual completion mixtures certify their worst-case normalized expected length.

source_refs.claim: Exact intervals under interference can be obtained by optimizing over compatible potential-outcome completions, but exhaustive evaluation is exponential and remains conservative.
source_refs.author: Joseph Rigdon and Michael G. Hudgens

source_refs.venue: Proceedings of the 24th International Conference on Machine Learning

source_refs.excerpt: Define a rectangular, history-tree-indexed completion object: fix potential outcomes ex ante
Add a worked K=3 primal--dual certificate at one small n

open_problems.why_unsolved: Completion-based exact inference and finite confidence-set games supply separate ingredients, but neither constructs the correct state space for a continuous four-matrix schedule observed through two balanced assignments. Independently optimized cellwise or assignmentwise completions need not come from one globally fixed potential-outcome schedule. The first required step is therefore a lossless quotient of global schedule completions by observational equivalence that preserves row, column, interaction, and counterfactual ambiguity. The resulting quantized game must also carry certified coverage, policy-approximation, and cross-n errors; a generic finite LP without those guarantees does not resolve the opportunity.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Explicit rational primal-dual programs returning an observed-table interval policy and an admissible least-favourable completion mixture, with necessary-and-sufficient global compatibility constraints and a computable error bound tending to zero.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing connects missing potential outcomes, compatible completions, exact inversion, computational explosion, and the need for narrower procedures.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Interference multiplies the missing potential outcomes -> validity requires protection against every compatible completion -> exhaustive completion enumeration is costly and conservative -> build a certified finite game for continuous four-exposure two-sided data.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent coverage-constrained expected-size optimization as a bilinear zero-sum game, solve a finite discretization by linear programming, and use primal-dual gaps as certificates.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired upper policy and all-interval lower certificate are naturally the two sides of the same decision game.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent unobserved joint potential-outcome dependence as a multi-marginal optimal-transport problem and prove sharpness through primal-dual coupling arguments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both settings optimize over missing cross-world couplings; the MRD destination adds global balanced-assignment compatibility.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive the least-favourable-prior dual of minimax expected confidence-set measure by calibrated test inversion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the decision-theoretic equality needed to turn a dual completion mixture into a lower certificate against every interval.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the alignment-aware Gaussian-chaos limit boundary of the balanced two-sided MRD contrast when coordinate influences vanish but the interaction operator norm remains a nonvanishing fraction of the design scale.

source_refs.claim: Low-degree, low-influence functions have close distributions on a fixed-weight Boolean slice, the Boolean cube, and Gaussian space.
source_refs.author: Yuval Filmus, Guy Kindler, Elchanan Mossel, and Karl Wimmer

source_refs.claim: Explicit invariance bounds for homogeneous sums transfer Gaussian and non-Gaussian Wiener-chaos criteria under low coordinate influence.

source_refs.excerpt: State a quantitative rate for the weighted Gaussian transport modulus epsilon_G

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing MRD arguments condition on one population and seek a conditional linear CLT plus concentration of its random variance, suppressing the regime in which singular directions of the bilinear term survive and align with the linear buyer and seller terms. Slice invariance and homogeneous-sum universality justify replacement in adjacent models, but neither identifies the joint canonical parameters formed by singular values and the projections of a and b onto their singular vectors. The replacement must also control nonsmooth coverage and truncated-length functionals, not only smooth expectations or the marginal law of a fixed statistic.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform quantitative approximation of a^T r+b^T s+r^T C s by its shared-coordinate Gaussian analogue, together with a necessary-and-sufficient characterization of every aligned Gaussian-plus-finite-rank subsequential limit and its normal subregime.

writing_exemplar.why: Its design-based CLT narrative makes the destination a boundary of MRD inference rather than an isolated probability theorem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Two balanced randomizations create nonstandard dependence -> existing inference is Gaussian when no component dominates -> low coordinate influence can coexist with spectrally concentrated bilinear variation -> characterize the full aligned Gaussian-chaos boundary.

method_exemplars.technique: Transport low-degree functions from a balanced slice through their harmonic multilinear representation using a low-influence invariance bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The independent buyer and seller assignments are fixed-weight slices, and the full error is one degree-two polynomial with shared coordinates.

method_exemplars.technique: Use replacement inequalities and Wiener-chaos contraction criteria to separate Gaussian limits from persistent non-Gaussian homogeneous sums.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After slice replacement, the interaction is a second Gaussian chaos whose nonnormality is spectral rather than coordinatewise.

method_exemplars.technique: Diagonalize a Gaussian quadratic-plus-linear form and invert its characteristic function with explicit truncation control.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The aligned limit is representable as a noncentral indefinite quadratic form, enabling calibration without assuming normality.

open_problems.open_problem: Prove a same-experiment decision-risk transfer from balanced half-sampling completion subexperiments to Gaussian linear-plus-bilinear limit experiments that preserves uniform coverage and normalized expected interval length.

source_refs.claim: The paper bounds Le Cam distance between multivariate hypergeometric and Gaussian experiments, but not for fixed-half product slices with schedule-dependent bilinear chaos.
source_refs.author: Frédéric Ouimet

source_refs.claim: Finite-population randomization CLTs give distributional convergence but not two-way Markov kernels or minimax transfer for arbitrary interval policies.
source_refs.author: Xinran Li and Peng Ding
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.excerpt: Develop the converse handle into an explicit nuisance-rich schedule family

open_problems.why_unsolved: A CLT or Kolmogorov approximation for the contrast cannot lower-bound every interval based on the full observed table. Existing hypergeometric Le Cam bounds do not cover fixed one-half sampling in a product of two slices with schedule-dependent chaos, and the prior converse failure shows that omitted nuisance coordinates can make a supposedly hidden parameter observable. The first proof step must construct two-way comparison kernels or a direct risk coupling for a nuisance-rich family that preserves the entire observation law. Because interval length is unbounded, experiment comparison must also be combined with truncation and uniform-integrability bounds derived from bounded outcomes.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit o(1) deficiency or two-sided risk-comparison bound between admissible finite MRD completion experiments and an aligned Gaussian-chaos experiment, with uniform transfer inequalities for coverage and Vplus-normalized expected length over all interval policies.

writing_exemplar.why: Its setup highlights the distinction between approximating a designated MRD statistic and comparing the full experiment needed for minimax optimality.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: An MRD contrast has a tractable randomization law -> Gaussian approximation validates a chosen procedure -> optimality quantifies over every function of the observed table -> obtain an experiment-level risk transfer for all interval policies.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct jittering and rounding Markov kernels and bound their total-variation error through a local likelihood-ratio expansion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Balanced complete randomization is sampling without replacement; the missing extension is to fixed sampling fraction and a product-slice table.

method_exemplars.technique: Couple a fixed-weight slice to Gaussian space while preserving low-degree polynomial evaluations under low influence.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The transfer must retain the buyer-seller degree-two statistic rather than approximate isolated hypergeometric counts.

method_exemplars.technique: Express expected confidence-set measure through acceptance probabilities so approximation error can be propagated at decision-risk level.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested transfer concerns precisely the coverage and expected-length losses in the minimax value.

open_problems.open_problem: Quantify the unavoidable honest-length adaptation cost when the four population exposure variances defining Vplus are not uniformly recoverable from the realized MRD table, including the rho=0 additive boundary.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The closest bipartite work separates an observable conservative envelope from exact potential-outcome variance, but Vplus here combines four population exposure variances and the table reveals neither all component schedules nor their cross-world dependence. A canceled row or column component can defeat relative-error variance estimation even when rho=0, so plug-in spectral calibration is not uniformly justified. The missing object is an observed-table completion modulus comparing schedules with nearly identical data laws but different normalizing envelopes, together with a policy that adapts without using true Vplus.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact oracle-to-observable adaptation value, expressed through a finite completion modulus or limiting experiment, with an explicit observed-table interval attaining it and an indistinguishable-schedule lower bound normalized by each schedule's true Vplus.

writing_exemplar.why: It distinguishes observable design information from latent finite-population variance in the closest bipartite experimental setting.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Bipartite exposure means are policy-relevant -> design variance depends on an incompletely observed fixed schedule -> operational inference needs an observable certificate -> quantify the sharp interval-length price of replacing the oracle envelope.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive attained extremal covariance bounds from observable marginals and invert the upper endpoint into conservative design-based inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the canonical oracle-to-observable variance-envelope argument, although the MRD completion geometry is four-way and crossed.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct an observable conservative variance proxy under interference by randomized deletion and analyze its gap from oracle variance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It confronts hidden covariance using only randomized observed data, while the destination asks for the exact expected-length cost.

method_exemplars.technique: Use a bipartite Hájek decomposition, conservative variance construction, and randomization CLT for exposure-dependent outcomes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its observation channel and design-based estimand are closest to the four-exposure marketplace destination.

literature_map:
Bajari et al. (2023, Statistical Science, DOI 10.1214/23-STS883) motivate multiple randomization as a way to identify marketplace spillovers that ordinary A/B tests cannot separate.
Masoero et al. (2026, JRSSB, DOI 10.1093/jrsssb/qkaf073; arXiv:2112.13495) give four-exposure SMRD estimators, exact component variances, conservative variance estimators, and quantitative CLTs.
The central MRD tension is that observed exposure outcomes support conservative inference, while cross-exposure covariance and the aligned interaction law depend on jointly unobserved schedules.
Sudijono et al. (2026, arXiv:2603.19480) derive estimable regression adjustments and improved CLTs for double randomization, but optimize estimator variance rather than all-policy honest interval length.
Liu, Shaikh, and Toulis (2025, arXiv:2504.06215) provide exact sharp-null and studentized weak-null tests for two-sided markets, not minimax interval-length optimization over composite schedules.
Hudgens and Halloran (2008, JASA, DOI 10.1198/016214508000000292) and Liu and Hudgens (2014, JASA, DOI 10.1080/01621459.2013.844698) are foundational design-based interference and large-sample interval anchors.
Rigdon and Hudgens (2015, Statistics & Probability Letters, DOI 10.1016/j.spl.2015.06.011) invert tests over compatible completions, document computational explosion, and call for narrower exact intervals.
Aronow, Green, and Lee (2014, Annals of Statistics, DOI 10.1214/13-AOS1200; arXiv:1405.6555) obtain sharp one-population variance bounds via extremal couplings, contrasting with MRD's richer four-schedule ambiguity.
Li and Ding (2017, JASA, DOI 10.1080/01621459.2017.1295865) and Shi and Ding (2022, arXiv:2209.12345) provide finite-population CLT and Berry-Esseen tools for linear randomization statistics, not persistent finite-rank bilinear chaos.
Filmus et al. (2018, ACM TOCT, DOI 10.1145/3186590; arXiv:1504.01689) give low-influence invariance on a balanced slice, the natural replacement tool for buyer and seller half-samples.
Nourdin, Peccati, and Reinert (2010, Annals of Probability, DOI 10.1214/10-AOP531; arXiv:0904.1153) distinguish Gaussian and non-Gaussian homogeneous-sum limits through Wiener-chaos machinery.
Ouimet (2022, Results in Mathematics, DOI 10.1007/s00025-021-01575-3; arXiv:2107.11565) supplies hypergeometric-to-Gaussian Le Cam kernels, but not fixed-half product-slice transfer for unbounded interval risk.
Evans, Hansen, and Stark (2005, Bernoulli, DOI 10.3150/bj/1126126761) and Bryan et al. (2007, ICML, DOI 10.1145/1273496.1273509) turn minimax expected confidence-set size into a least-favourable-prior game and finite LP.
Imhof (1961, Biometrika, DOI 10.1093/biomet/48.3-4.419) and Davies (1980, Applied Statistics, DOI 10.2307/2346911) provide certified characteristic-function algorithms for Gaussian quadratic-form probabilities.
Comola and Prina (2023, Economic Journal, DOI 10.1093/ej/ueac053) supply the bilateral savings-network application later reanalyzed by Liu-Shaikh-Toulis.
